newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Call for truth commission in Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: Call for truth commission in Mozambique.

text.p: The parliamentary group of Mozambique's former rebel movement on Monday called for the establishment of a "truth commission" to investigate atrocities committed during the civil war between 1976 and 1992.
David Alone, the deputy head of the Renamo grouping, said the proposed body would hear testimony on war crimes from witnesses who would then be pardoned.
The call follows bitter clashes in parliament last Thursday when deputies from Renamo and from the majority Frelimo Party blamed each other for war atrocities.
During these angry exchanges, Frelimo deputy Lina Magaia expressed regret that no truth commission had ever been set up in Mozambique.
South Africa set up such a commission to deal with apartheid-era crimes after President Nelson Mandela was elected in 1994 in the country's first all-race elections.
Alone said on Monday that parliament should "consider seriously the possibility and necessity of creating a truth and reconciliation commission".

He said a truth body was needed "so that the Mozambican people may know the full truth of the executions and massacres perpetrated by the dictatorial Frelimo regime, and possibly by those who fought for democracy" -- by which he meant Renamo.
Although the crimes committed "cry out for justice", he said that "the assassins and butchers will not be punished after they have been heard by the commission".
